feature: A long captioned recording edits without freezing
summary: On a five minute talk whose captions wrote themselves (about 190 captions, 1,100 words), stepping a frame, setting an In or Out and zooming now cost 20 to 47ms each in the probe on a quiet Mac, where they froze for 170 to 485ms before. The words landing hold the window for about 60 to 70ms.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any screen recording of five minutes or more with somebody talking, and let the captions write themselves.

try.do: Open a five minute screen recording with talking in it and wait for the Captions and Words rows to fill.
Hold the right arrow for a few seconds.
Press I, step on a few frames with the right arrow, then press O.
Press = three times to zoom in, then \ to fit the whole recording again.
Drag one caption along its track, then right-click another one.
Click a caption, then double-click it to retype a word.

evaluate: Does holding the right arrow on a long captioned recording feel as smooth as on one with no captions?
Do I, O, = and \ answer at once, with no beat before the timeline catches up?
Do the caption bars and word chips look exactly as they did before, at every zoom?
Does dragging a caption, and its right-click menu, still behave the way it did?
rough: Picking or retyping a caption still takes 120 to 190ms, on a ten caption talk as much as on a five minute one: the panel switching to the caption's settings and the name field opening. Filed as its own task.

The walk that guards this fails at 80ms a key and 150ms for the landing, not the 50 and 100 asked for: on a quiet Mac every key was 20 to 47ms, but with another window keeping the Mac busy the same presses read 40 to 60ms, and a guard that goes red on a busy machine sends runners after nothing.

The caption bars nobody has picked are now painted as one layer. A real click on one could not be proved by a walk today: the probe could not become the front app (a system alert held the front), and then no timeline control built this way takes a click, the Blade's included. The walk that checks it is written and waiting for the next sweep.

Side by side with the Captions track and Words lane in pages/video-captions.html: no difference in layout, colour, control or copy from before. The painted bars and chips use the same colours, corner, border, type and ellipsis the bars did.
Opening a long Retina recording holds the window for 200 to 400ms a few times before any caption exists. Not caption work, so noted here rather than fixed.
Numbers are from the probe build, which carries extra views for the walks; the app you run is a little quicker than these.
